scams.name: The Samarkand Railway Taxi Mob
scams.tldr: They open with 300,000 UZS for a ride to the Registan area — about $24, ten times the fair price.
scams.description: They open with 300,000 UZS for a ride to the Registan area — about $24, ten times the fair price. The crowd is dense, six or seven men deep, and the loudest of them follows you across the parking lot, grabbing at your suitcase handle. He insists 300,000 is the 'official rate.' Two of his associates flank you, blocking the path toward the taxi line further out. The encounter is calibrated to break first-time-arrival composure, and most travelers either cave to the inflated quote or negotiate down to 150,000–200,000 UZS, still 5–7x the fair rate.
scams.avoidance: Try Yandex Go app despite inconsistent coverage -- it sometimes works. Walk 100 meters past the taxi crowd to the main road and flag a regular car. The fair price to Registan is 20,000-30,000 UZS -- don't pay more. Arrange airport/station pickup through your hotel in advance. Have the Uzbek for 'how much to Registan?' ready on your phone translator.
scams.location: Samarkand Railway Station arrivals exit, the parking forecourt, the unofficial pickup zone past the official rank

scams.name: The Registan Silk Carpet 'Certificate' Markup
scams.tldr: After twenty minutes of warm conversation, he produces a 'certificate of authenticity' in Cyrillic script, claiming the carpet is genuine Samarkand silk, hand-knotted by a master weaver in Khujand, certified by the Uzbek Crafts Union, and worth $2,000.
scams.description: After twenty minutes of warm conversation, he produces a 'certificate of authenticity' in Cyrillic script, claiming the carpet is genuine Samarkand silk, hand-knotted by a master weaver in Khujand, certified by the Uzbek Crafts Union, and worth $2,000. He pulls out a calculator. The 'special tourist price' he offers is $500 — a quarter of the supposed value. He frames it as an opportunity. You feel the social weight of having drunk three cups of his tea.
scams.avoidance: Visit the Samarkand Bukhara Silk Carpets Factory to see real production and fair prices. If you want a carpet, compare prices at multiple non-tourist shops first. Haggle aggressively -- offer one-third of the asking price. A Cyrillic certificate proves nothing about authenticity. Know that genuine handmade silk carpets start at $100+ per square meter at fair prices.
scams.location: Carpet shops inside and around Registan Square, the souvenir corridor of Siab Bazaar, the strip near Bibi-Khanym Mosque

scams.name: The Registan Unofficial-Guide Shakedown
scams.tldr: His English is fluent, his manner is warm, and within minutes he is sharing genuinely interesting facts about Ulugh Beg's astronomical madrasa, the symbolism of the Sher-Dor lions on the second madrasa's iwan, and the Tilya-Kori's gold-leaf interior.
scams.description: His English is fluent, his manner is warm, and within minutes he is sharing genuinely interesting facts about Ulugh Beg's astronomical madrasa, the symbolism of the Sher-Dor lions on the second madrasa's iwan, and the Tilya-Kori's gold-leaf interior. The information is real, the delivery is engaging, and you feel like you are learning more than a guidebook would offer. The walk takes about an hour, the photo stops are well-chosen, and you genuinely enjoy the experience.
scams.avoidance: Hire licensed guides wearing official Uzbektourism badges. Agree on the exact price before the tour starts -- in writing if needed. Approach the Tourist Police at Registan if you feel pressured. Pay only after the tour is complete and you're satisfied. Explore with a guidebook or audio guide from your hotel instead.
scams.location: Registan Square entrance, the surrounding plaza, the corridors between the three madrasas, the corner near the audio-guide booth

scams.name: The Siab Bazaar Tourist-Price Quote
scams.tldr: A vendor in the souvenir section calls you over to admire embroidered suzani textiles and small ceramic pieces.
scams.description: A vendor in the souvenir section calls you over to admire embroidered suzani textiles and small ceramic pieces. He glances at you, takes you in for half a second, and quotes 200,000 UZS for a small ceramic plate. The price feels high but plausible for handmade work, and you nod. What you do not see is that the same vendor sold an identical plate to a Samarkand grandmother an hour earlier for 70,000 UZS — the price was set the moment you opened your mouth in a foreign accent.
scams.avoidance: Offer one-third of the first quoted price and negotiate from there. Watch the scale carefully -- ask them to zero it before weighing. Buy non bread and fresh items from the local food section, not the tourist side. Compare prices with at least three vendors before buying. Bring your own small bag so vendors can't add unwanted items.
scams.location: Siab Bazaar (Siyob Bozor) next to Bibi-Khanym Mosque, the covered souvenir section, the dried-fruit and nut aisles, the bread-and-spice corridor

scams.name: The Samarkand Attraction Entrance-Fee Inconsistency
scams.tldr: You pay, take the small printed ticket, and walk through the gate.
scams.description: You pay, take the small printed ticket, and walk through the gate. Later that afternoon, talking to another traveler at your guesthouse, you discover she paid 25,000 UZS at the same site that morning — half what you paid. The ticket seller had quoted her 25,000 directly when she stood at the booth; he quoted you 50,000 with the same casual confidence and the same printed ticket.
scams.avoidance: Research entrance fees on recent travel blogs before visiting each site. Ask to see the official price list before paying. Request a printed ticket or receipt for every payment. The Registan entrance is officially 50,000 UZS -- use that as a benchmark. Ask your hotel reception for current entrance fees to plan your budget.
scams.location: Bibi-Khanym Mosque, Shah-i-Zinda necropolis, Ulugh Beg Observatory, Gur-e-Amir Mausoleum, smaller heritage sites without posted price boards

scams.name: The Samarkand Guesthouse Bait-and-Switch
scams.tldr: When you arrive after the train from Tashkent, the host welcomes you warmly and shows you to a room that looks nothing like the photos.
scams.description: When you arrive after the train from Tashkent, the host welcomes you warmly and shows you to a room that looks nothing like the photos. The room is smaller, dirtier, has no air conditioning despite the listing promising it, and the bathroom is shared rather than private. The host explains that the 'nice room' you saw in the listing is currently taken by another guest, and offers you this room at the same price — or, alternatively, a 'proper' room with the listing's amenities for $45 per night.
scams.avoidance: Book through platforms with free cancellation so you can walk away. Read the most recent reviews, not just the overall rating. Message the hotel the day before to reconfirm your exact room. Have a backup accommodation option identified in case of bait-and-switch. Pay through the platform only -- never agree to cash-only demands.
scams.location: Budget guesthouses and B&Bs near Registan, the area around Bibi-Khanym Mosque, the historic city walking-tour districts, booked via Booking.com or Airbnb
